question: What is the UK National Living Wage hourly rate for workers aged 21 and over from April 2026?
answer:
The UK National Living Wage for workers aged 21 and over is £12.71 per hour from 1 April 2026, up from £12.21 [1][2]. The increase of 50p (4.1%) was accepted in full by the Government from the Low Pay Commission's recommendations [2]. It is set in the National Minimum Wage Regulations 2015 as amended, which came into force on 1 April 2026 and extend to England and Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland [6]. Workers in their first year of an apprenticeship are not covered by this rate [1].

This is general legal information about UK rules only, and rules differ in other jurisdictions. A person's specific situation, such as a suspected underpayment, needs a licensed lawyer. The sources point to Acas for free advice and to HMRC for reporting underpayment [1][5].

keyPoints.text: The National Living Wage for workers aged 21 and over is £12.71 per hour from 1 April 2026.
The rate rose by 50p (4.1%) from the previous £12.21 rate that applied until 31 March 2026.
The increase was set under the Low Pay Commission's recommendations and enacted by regulation effective 1 April 2026.
Workers aged 21 and over who are not in their first year of an apprenticeship are legally entitled to at least this rate.

mayBeStale.text: Source 2's publication date (November 2025) and source 4's forward-looking 2027 estimates predate the current rate and are not the operative figure for April 2026.
Source 5 shows an April 2025 agricultural rate table with the old £12.21 NLW figure, which is superseded for the NLW itself.
